frontier.hypothesis: The one untried mechanism-level lever is to remove (s32)r4 - K from loop.c's movable set by making it not loop-invariant, so a single-set fresh carrier stays inside the loop and reproduces the winning single-set, single-use, REG_DEAD RTL shape without a multi-write carrier.
frontier.mechanism: loop.c:1631 moves a movable when threshold * savings * lifetime >= insn_count; loop.c:532 fixes threshold; loop.c:790-793 fix savings and lifetime. Every measured spelling so far changes the set count only. If invariant_p does not accept the base's source expression, no movable is recorded at all and the +2 disappears.
frontier.next_probe: Run tmp/grind/func_8005D554/run_dump.sh on tmp/grind/func_8005D554/s5b/enum2/fresh_direct_before.c and read the .loop dump's movable list for this loop to get the recorded lifetime, savings and insn_count numbers; then search for a source spelling of the base whose value invariant_p rejects while cse.c/combine.c fold the emitted arithmetic back to the same addiu -- e.g. deriving the -K displacement through a loop-written location.

frontier.hypothesis: The object model at the p_b2e0 = (u8 *)&D_8009B2E0 declaration pun is the last untried STRUCTURAL axis; a real struct type with a member for the +0xC sub-object changes which insns exist in the setup block and therefore the INSN_LUID sequence the sched1 tie-break reads.
frontier.mechanism: The typed-array spelling (H3) was killed at 21 because array indexing re-derives idx*60 + base per use; a base POINTER to a struct with an explicit sub-object member keeps stride in s0 and base+0xC+stride in the frame slot the way the byte-pointer model does, while changing the setup block's insn set.
frontier.next_probe: Declare the struct type TU-locally in src/text1b.c purely to MEASURE (a TU-local aggregate is excluded by the aggregate-merge family's header-canonical prong, so it cannot be submitted as-is); sweep it against the candidate. Only if it scores below 6 is the header route + integration handoff worth opening.

frontier.hypothesis: The s.zero10 output-dependence route -- the only construct that has ever measured below 6 (the permuter's sandbox-3 find) -- may still be reachable through a value the program genuinely stages, now that parameters and dead locals are measured out.
frontier.mechanism: s1's exact scheduler model (tmp/grind/func_8005D554/s1/mutate_out.txt, case launch_dep228) predicts the target order when the a2-base set and the s.zero10 store share a destination pseudo. The permuter reaches it with an invented multi-write local, which the Judge banned on 2026-09-08.
frontier.next_probe: This session confirmed func_80073728 reads +0x10 as a real input (asm/funcs/func_80073728.s:314), so a program-motivated carrier for that store is unlikely; before spending more here, re-check whether the 0x1C field (the a2 site) and the 0x10 field are ever written from the same source value elsewhere in text1b.c's sibling callers of func_80073728, and if no caller does, treat this route as closed and put the next session's weight on frontier item 1.

judge_constraints: No fresh (invented) local may be written more than once to act as a staging carrier for the a2-site base `(s32)r4 - K` or for any other value in this function, under any name; the existing-local borrow quadrant (staged-value-reused-variable, all six bounds) and the alternate-chassis route (frontier item 2, e.g. the z3 guard-duplicated while) remain open.
